correctness.rationale: The full tent iterate has one fixed point per dyadic monotonicity interval with the displayed exact rational coordinates. For prime p, the only lower periods are one, removing exactly 0 and 2/3. For p odd the deletion index q=(2N-1)/3 is odd; after applying the two-rank formula on either side, all four parity/rank inequalities prove D*=2/(N+1), with equality at the first surviving point. The monotone quantile coupling is a constructive W_infty upper bound and any coupling must obey quantile mass inequalities, giving equality. Quantile intervals also cover [0,1] at the same radius; x=0 provides the lower bound. Standard tight Lipschitz upper/lower envelopes and functions ±L dist(x,P_p) establish minimax equality. p=2 is checked directly. Adjacent grid gap formulas plus removal of q prove the exact largest internal gap. The included standalone exact-rational verifier passed 41,669 checks, but is supplementary rather than proof.

value.rationale: The complete least-prime-period point set is precisely the finite object singled out by recent qualitative interval-map rigidity results. The theorem determines its exact spatial resolution, quantile transport and global star discrepancy simultaneously, identifies the missing-endpoint obstruction, and yields a sharp minimax recovery error for every Lipschitz observable. The calculation is nontrivial because deleting the nonzero fixed point shifts ranks and makes composite-period analogues fail (n=6). This is a natural, parameter-uniform quantitative classification of finite prime-orbit data rather than a one-off count or substitution into a standard estimate.
